notes: Board of Park Commissioners minutes, 1932. Curated: the Coit Memorial Tower (Supervisors' resolution, Art Commission approval, contract award and the revised design) and the Park Police stables.

coverage.remaining: Not placed: the Aquatic Park recreation pier continued by Healy-Tibbitts ($125,000, Bakewell & Brown and John A. Baur, engineers Frank G. White and Harry E. Squire), the Gold Star Mothers' boulder in Heroes' Grove, the City Attorney's opinion that Ordinance 18009 (1915) dedicated the Civic Center lands to park use, P. O. Tognelli's $350 scale model of the Coit Tower, the AIA's protest against a statuary group on Telegraph Hill.
coverage.note: Ten meetings held (Jan 21, Feb 11, Apr 8, May 19, Jun 2, Aug 5, Sep 1, Sep 22, Oct 13, Dec 22); the rest postponed for want of a quorum. Dated by the opener 'was held ... on Thursday, <date>'. Curated list PB1932.py.

findings.description: The Board of Park Commissioners had let the architect W. P. Day build the foundations, columns, walls, floors and roof of the stables for the new Park Police Station with park forces for up to $8,000; told the funds would not stretch to that, it rescinded the order and had Assistant Superintendent Earl Clements build half of the stall structure, enough for about twenty horses.

findings.address_as_written: Resolution of the Board of Supervisors No. 325 re Coit Memorial
findings.description: The Board of Park Commissioners received the Supervisors' resolution that the roughly $125,000 Lillie Hitchcock Coit left the city for adding to its beauty be spent on a tower on Telegraph Hill, to be called the Coit Memorial Tower, asking the Park Commission to permit it on its land at the top of the hill and to have plans prepared and contracts let.

findings.address_as_written: Resolutions Nos. 1-3 - award of contract, Telegraph Hill tower
findings.description: The Board of Park Commissioners awarded Young & Horstmeyer, low bidders, the contract to build the Coit Memorial Tower for $100,507, their bid with alternates one, four and six, the sixth adding about 26 feet 3 inches to the shaft with the extra footings and steel it needed; it set aside up to $3,800 more for the changes the Art Commission had demanded, and agreed to pay Arthur Brown, Jr. for architecture, engineering and inspection out of the Coit Memorial Fund.

findings.description: To meet the Art Commission's demands, Arthur Brown, Jr. reported, the tower had been made taller, its base cut down to a bare octagon, the flutes of the shaft reduced from 32 to 24, the restaurant, kitchen, store room and boiler room taken out, the south terrace reduced to a rim around the building, a cast stone balustrade put in place of a plain wall with three cast stone ornaments over the front door, and a gas supply added for a flare at the top.
